external_entities.name: Colleagues
external_entities.description: Internal colleagues who sign in through the identity broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
external_entities.notes: Colleagues sign in from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

external_entities.name: Franchise colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues from franchise stores who authenticate through their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The HR system that supplies colleague group membership changes and leaver changes.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

external_entities.name: Identity provider
external_entities.description: The identity provider used by franchise colleagues to vouch for them.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The source does not state which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

processes.name: Identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, validates federated sign-ins, and synchronizes colleague and group information.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The broker runs on the corporate network. It does not call back to check whether a colleague is still allowed in after issuing a token. Nobody has written down whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: Store admin console
processes.description: An application that uses token groups to authorize price changes and transaction voids across stores.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: Key store
data_stores.description: A key store holding the broker's token-signing key.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: Directory
data_stores.description: The broker's directory of colleagues and their groups.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: Audit log
data_stores.description: The audit log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records, whether it covers the franchise route, or whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: Colleagues sign in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The broker issues a token that the console uses for authorization.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token carries the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing the colleague's staff id and groups

data_flows.name: franchise sign-in
data_flows.description: Franchise colleagues sign in through the broker using a federated identity assertion.
data_flows.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.
data_flows.notes: The franchise route is described further as the franchise identity provider vouching for franchise colleagues and the broker taking that as a sign-in.

data_flows.name: vouch for colleague
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague to the broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
data_flows.notes: The source does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: Applications fetch the public half of the signing key from the broker to check token signatures.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.notes: The source describes applications generally; the store admin console is one of those applications.
data_flows.data_description: Public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: pull group changes
data_flows.description: The broker pulls colleague and group membership changes from the HR system overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night
data_flows.notes: The same overnight changes are also how leavers stop being colleagues.

data_flows.name: update directory
data_flows.description: The broker maintains colleague and group membership data in its directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: keep signing key
data_flows.description: The broker keeps its token-signing key in the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.
trust_boundaries.notes: The store admin console also runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: Colleagues' own devices at home
trust_boundaries.description: The home-device environment from which colleagues may sign in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: Franchise stores
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise-store environment whose colleagues are allowed to sign in through their own identity provider.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console presents a web interface because the source calls it a console.
assumptions.basis: The source names the component as the 'store admin console'; consoles are treated as web interfaces under the extraction rules.

assumptions.assumption: The key store's contents are confidential because it holds a token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store holds the broker's signing key, which is a secret.

assumptions.assumption: The directory's contents are confidential because it holds colleague identities and group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory holds colleagues and the groups they are in, identifying and describing people.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log's contents are confidential because it holds sign-in records.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the audit log records sign-ins, which are records about colleagues' authentication activity.
